title: A scalable entanglement distribution framework for hybrid quantum networks
authors: Yaqi Zhao, Kan He, Jinchuan Hou, Yongtao Zhang, Nicolò Lo Piparo, Xiangyi Meng
abstract: The realization of a scalable quantum network (QN) hinges on the efficient distribution of entanglement across heterogeneous hardware platforms. While traditional QN frameworks are often restricted to single-encoding schemes, relying exclusively on either discrete (DV) or continuous (CV) variables, such segregated architectures limit the capacity and interoperability of large-scale systems. Here, we propose a scalable hybrid entanglement distribution scheme that bridges these domains by mapping hybrid entanglement swapping and concentration at DV-CV interfaces onto a unified set of series and parallel graph rules. We demonstrate that our hybrid approach exhibits a potential performance advantage over traditional point-to-point generation of maximally entangled states, achieving enhanced end-to-end entanglement within series-parallel topologies. These results provide a robust theoretical foundation for designing resource-efficient, interpretable architectures for the future quantum internet.
summary: This paper proposes a scalable theoretical framework for distributing entanglement in hybrid quantum networks that combine discrete-variable and continuous-variable quantum links. By unifying entanglement swapping and concentration rules onto graph theory principles, it shows that this hybrid approach can enhance end-to-end entanglement generation compared to traditional methods. This provides a crucial theoretical roadmap for building large-scale, interoperable quantum internet infrastructure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of creating a scalable entanglement distribution framework capable of operating across heterogeneous quantum hardware platforms that utilize both discrete (DV) and continuous (CV) variable entanglement.
main_result: The proposed hybrid entanglement distribution scheme demonstrates potential performance advantages over traditional point-to-point generation, particularly within series-parallel network topologies.
method: The authors developed a theoretical framework by mapping hybrid entanglement swapping and concentration protocols onto a unified set of series and parallel graph rules, utilizing homogeneous consolidation preprocessing.
model_or_system: The model is a Quantum Network (QN) composed of links representing bipartite entangled states, which can be either DV (two-qubit states) or CV (TMSVSs). The analysis focuses on network topologies like series-parallel and honeycomb lattices.
key_observables: Total Singlet Conversion Probability (SCP), Concurrence (c), and Ratio Negativity ($\chi_N$).
important_parameters: The performance is analyzed based on the structure of the network (series-parallel vs. non-series-parallel) and the specific hybrid swapping operations used (homodyne vs. majorization).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes ideal physical conditions, although the framework is designed to absorb realistic hardware imperfections into effective resource parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate various QN topologies (series-parallel vs. non-series-parallel) and detail the step-by-step process of homogeneous consolidation used to simplify the complex hybrid network structure.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for hybrid frameworks, then details the homogeneous consolidation strategy to reduce the network to an irreducible hybrid junction. It subsequently analyzes basic hybrid swapping protocols (homodyne and majorization) before presenting the final scalable protocol for series QNs.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental engineering challenge of integrating disparate quantum hardware modalities (DV and CV) into a single, scalable quantum internet architecture.
